title: Microsoft Purview Insider Risk Management: expanded user profile in alerts
summary: Hold: the briefing treats default profile visibility as undocumented even though Microsoft documents pseudonymisation by default and explicitly says it hides the expanded profile. It also says the attributes appear on every opened alert, contradicting that privacy gate. The documented controls, licensing and roadmap facts otherwise check out.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; Why it matters; Open questions: first question
claims.claim: Microsoft has not stated whether the expanded profile is visible when the Privacy setting has not been changed.
claims.quote: Built with privacy by design, users are pseudonymized by default ... When pseudo-anonymization is enabled, the expanded user profile details aren't visible.
claims.fix: Set defaultState to 'admin-opt-in'. Replace the uncertainty sentence with 'Users are pseudonymised by default, which hides the expanded profile; an administrator must turn off username anonymisation to expose it.' Remove the first Open questions bullet. The activities page states both the default and its effect; the cited Privacy page documents the administrator's setting.

claims.claim: The additional attributes appear on every alert a reviewer opens in the unified experience.
claims.quote: When pseudo-anonymization is enabled, the expanded user profile details aren't visible.
claims.fix: Delete 'and they appear on every alert a reviewer opens in the unified experience'. This unconditional assertion also conflicts with the page's own summary and privacy explanation.

claims.quote: Choosing this setting anonymizes all users with current and past policy matches and applies to all policies.

claims.claim: The Privacy control is at Microsoft Purview portal > Settings > Insider Risk Management > Privacy.
claims.quote: Select Settings in the upper-right corner of the page. Select Insider Risk Management to go to the Insider Risk Management settings. Select Privacy. Select the option you want, to show anonymized names or not.
claims.fix: Complete the path to the deciding option: 'Settings > Insider Risk Management > Privacy > Show anonymized versions of usernames'. The printed path is correct but stops on the setting's page.

The standard's review rating is for capabilities that change nothing until someone chooses them.
